preShowdown.title: The Lowest Floor
preShowdown.scene: A dust-grey landing inside the tower, one man standing beside a hanging rope
preShowdown.speaker: Tovin
dialogue: They said the bell keeper slept while half the south ward waited for a warning. That is the story they kept.
I was awake. The rope was dead in my hands, and nobody asked why.
You are here now. So I will tell you.

preShowdown.title: The Rope
preShowdown.scene: Tovin holds up a length of old rope. The top is cut clean.
preShowdown.speaker: Tovin
dialogue: Look at the top of it. A worn rope tears ragged. This one is clean through.
I pulled that rope until my hands gave out. It wasn't attached to anything.
Somebody stood on the tower walk above me and cut it. I never learned who.

preShowdown.title: What They Promised
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the rope coiled over his shoulder like a duty
preShowdown.speaker: Tovin
dialogue: The council promised me a Showdown. A public table, my deck against the man who inspected the tower, and my side of it entered in the Chronicle win or lose.
He never came. They moved the date, then moved it again, and then there was no city left to hold it in.
I complained about that bell for years. Small faults, half of them nothing, and I made every one sound urgent. When the rope was cut, nobody listened. I had helped teach them not to.

preShowdown.title: You Showed Up
preShowdown.scene: The landing, a stone table with two worn seats
preShowdown.speaker: Tovin
dialogue: So. You're here, and you carry a deck.
I was supposed to face the rope inspector at sundown, on the record. I'll take you instead.
Set your cards. Let's finish something.

defeat.title: The Watch Continues
defeat.scene: The landing, Tovin gathering the cards without hurry
defeat.speaker: Tovin
dialogue: No shame in it. I had an age of standing still to think about my openings.
The rope will still be here when you come back.
So will I.

firstVictory.title: There
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the last card face up between them
firstVictory.speaker: Tovin
dialogue: There.
That's all it was supposed to be. Two decks, one table, somebody writing it down.
Four hundred years of waiting, for one hour of cards.

firstVictory.title: The Record
firstVictory.scene: Tovin sets the cut rope down on the stone table
firstVictory.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: He puts the rope down carefully, the way a man sets down something he has carried too far.
For the first time, he steps away from it.

firstVictory.title: Finished
firstVictory.scene: The landing, lighter somehow, the dust settling
firstVictory.speaker: Tovin
dialogue: I lost. Write that down too. I don't care about that part.
I rang that bell for thirty years, and it never once mattered whether I won anything.
Somebody cut the rope from above. Whatever you climb into up there, remember which direction the cut came from.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.scene: The landing, the table already dealt
rematch.speaker: Tovin
dialogue: Not me this time. The tower kept our match, the way the Chronicle keeps a page.
Go on. Pull the rope again.

preShowdown.title: The Grain Floor
preShowdown.scene: A landing stacked with grain sacks gone grey with dust, a woman weighing nothing on a balance scale
preShowdown.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: Let us save time. Yes, I held grain in the famine year. No, I did not steal it. Buying early is not stealing.
The charge on this floor concerns a gate guard named Doran.
Start wherever you like. We will reach him soon enough.

preShowdown.title: The Accusation
preShowdown.scene: The landing, flour dust hanging in the lamplight
preShowdown.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: He was a gate guard. Grain went missing from my east store, nine sacks, then eleven. I accused him in the open market with the flour still under my fingernails.
It ruined him. They took his post and struck his name from the roll.
He challenged me to a Showdown that same night, in front of the whole market. The whole market heard him say it.

preShowdown.title: Never Answered
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the balance scale swaying slightly
preShowdown.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: He died before the table was set. The collapse came fast in his quarter.
He died with my accusation as the last public word about him. I have had four hundred years to hear how final it sounded.
I need someone across the table. You'll do.

preShowdown.title: Terms
preShowdown.scene: The landing, Vetta shuffling with a trader's quick hands
preShowdown.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: I'll play you as if you were him. Don't take it personally. I did nothing personally in my whole life.
One thing first, since you'll wonder about it later. The rations that year made no sense. I sold the granary the same figures every month, and every month the city was hungrier.
Somebody was eating, and it wasn't the people paying me. Cards.

defeat.title: The Renegotiation
defeat.scene: The landing, Vetta already restacking the deck
defeat.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: That's one to me. Shall we call it best of three? Everything in this city was negotiable except the weather.
Come back when your deck is worth my time. That's not cruelty. That's an invoice.

firstVictory.title: Paid in Full
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the scale finally still
firstVictory.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: There. Doran's challenge finally has an answer. Four hundred years late and played by proxy.
Write down my loss. I have already had my version.

firstVictory.title: The Truth
firstVictory.scene: The landing, Vetta looking at her own hands
firstVictory.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: I knew where the grain went. I suspected by the second week and I knew by the fourth.
He was carting it to the shelter by the kiln yards. There were children in there whose parents had gone below the city and not come back up.
If I had said that in the market, the inspectors would have opened my books, and my books had a second cellar in them. So I said thief instead. It was cheaper.

firstVictory.title: The Name
firstVictory.scene: The landing, dust drifting off the sacks like smoke
firstVictory.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: Do not forgive me because I admitted it. Admission costs me nothing now.
When you leave, say his name. Doran, of the east gate. He carried those sacks to children waiting for their parents.
I knew what he had done, and I called him a thief to save my second cellar.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.scene: The landing, the deck squared and waiting
rematch.speaker: Vetta
dialogue: The tower has brought the scale out again. Apparently settled is not the same as finished.
Come on, then. It remembers every bargain I used to win.

preShowdown.title: The Third Landing
preShowdown.scene: A landing with a courier's satchel on a hook, straps worn to thread, a young woman pacing
preShowdown.speaker: Aya
dialogue: Don't stand in the doorway. It makes the room smaller.
You came up from Vetta's floor. Did she tell you she was innocent? Everyone up here is innocent, ask anybody.
I'm not. Sit down.

preShowdown.title: The Route
preShowdown.scene: The landing, her hand resting on the satchel without looking at it
preShowdown.speaker: Aya
dialogue: I ran the north line the night of the evacuation. One message left in my bag, priority seal. The kind you die before you drop.
Two streets off my route, my brother's block was already coming down.
I left the route. I dug him out with my hands. It took the whole night.

preShowdown.title: The Cost
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the pacing stopped
preShowdown.speaker: Aya
dialogue: The message named a district that was supposed to move before dawn. It moved after dawn. You can count the cost yourself. The numbers are in the Chronicle.
At the muster afterward, an officer called me a coward. A coward. I ran toward the thing everyone else was running from.
I challenged him on the spot. The city fell before the table was ever set.

preShowdown.title: The Match
preShowdown.scene: The landing, Aya already cutting her deck one-handed
preShowdown.speaker: Aya
dialogue: So here's what you get from me. No stalling, no careful little walls. I spent my whole life being fast and one night being slow.
And since you're collecting stories on the way up, here's what the message said. The aqueduct under the sealed district had gone dry. Weeks of rain, and the channel was dry as a scroll.
Nobody ever explained to me where a river goes. Set your cards.

defeat.title: Too Slow
defeat.scene: The landing, Aya not even winded
defeat.speaker: Aya
dialogue: That one is mine.
Pack the satchel, check the seal, start again. That is how a courier gets home after a bad run.
Take your time. The table will be here.

firstVictory.title: Delivered
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the satchel finally hanging still
firstVictory.speaker: Aya
dialogue: Good. That is the table he never had to face.
That's the match he owed me. It doesn't fix one thing about that night.

firstVictory.title: The Answer
firstVictory.scene: The landing, Aya looking at her palms
firstVictory.speaker: Aya
dialogue: People always ask whether I'd do it again. I asked myself before you ever climbed these stairs.
I found my brother alive. A district of strangers lost the hours I spent finding him. Both of those are true at once, and they don't settle.
Anyone who says they know what they'd have done was never on that street.

firstVictory.title: Go On Up
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the stairs waiting
firstVictory.speaker: Aya
dialogue: Call me a courier, not a coward. I finished every run I ever started except one, and now I've finished this.
The floors above me get worse. The people up there made their choices at desks, with seals and witnesses.
Mine at least fit in two hands.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.scene: The landing, the satchel packed again
rematch.speaker: Aya
dialogue: The tower runs my route now. It doesn't get tired, and it doesn't have a brother.
See if you can keep up with the memory. I couldn't.

preShowdown.title: The Records Floor
preShowdown.scene: A landing walled with pigeonhole shelves, one ledger open on a stand, a neat man squaring its corners
preShowdown.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: Before we begin, a correction. The plaque downstairs says I falsified thirty entries. It was twenty-six.
If they're going to hang a man's name on a number, the number should at least be right.
You've come to play the record closed. Good. Sit. Mind the ink.

preShowdown.title: The Entries
preShowdown.scene: The landing, his finger resting on one scraped line
preShowdown.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: The rations ran short in the third year. Not evenly short. The hill wards kept their full measure, and the kiln wards starved by a fifth.
I moved twenty-six entries. Grain that existed on paper in the hills began existing, on paper, by the kilns. Then it existed in fact. Paper is upstream of bread. Most people never learn that.
For that part, I would sign my name again today.

preShowdown.title: Marrek
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the lamplight catching one empty stool beside the stand
preShowdown.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: When the audit came, I gave them Marrek.
The seat next to mine for eleven years. He counted through his nose when the columns ran long. I hated the sound by the second winter.
I could have moved the entries so they traced to no one. It was three strokes more work. I chose the version with his name in the margin, and I told myself it was haste.

preShowdown.title: The Appointment
preShowdown.scene: The landing, Ansel closing the ledger with both hands
preShowdown.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: I requested a public Showdown to confess. The date was set. I stood outside the hall, counted the crowd through the doorway, and walked home.
A clerk who missed his own appointment. That's the whole of me, if you want it small.

One more entry for your collection, since you're climbing. The demand I was balancing against? The works below the city drew four men's rations for every man on their roll. And the men who came up from there could not always tell me their own names. Now. Cards.

defeat.title: A Correction
defeat.scene: The landing, Ansel noting something small in the margin
defeat.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: That result stands. No amendment required.
I will square the cards and wait. I am very good at both.

firstVictory.title: Entered
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the ledger open to a fresh page
firstVictory.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: So that is what it feels like from the losing chair. Marrek never got to sit in either one.
Record it. All of it. The twenty-six, and the kilns, and his name.

firstVictory.title: The Confession
firstVictory.scene: The landing, his hands flat on the stand for once
firstVictory.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: Do not make this kinder than it was. Feeding the kiln wards did not require me to ruin Marrek.
I moved the grain because it was right. I marked his name because, after eleven years, I wanted never to hear him count beside me again. The audit gave me the chance.
For centuries I joined those choices into one excuse. They were separate, and both were mine.

firstVictory.title: Adjournment
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the stool beside him pushed neatly in
firstVictory.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: If Marrek has family somewhere down the years, tell them he did not alter those entries. I did.
Twenty-six changes fed a ward. One extra mark destroyed him.
Do not let the first fact excuse the second.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.speaker: Ansel
dialogue: The tower has my columns memorized. It even counts through its nose. I have decided to find that funny.
Audit the memory as often as you like. The figures will not move.

preShowdown.title: The Infirmary Floor
preShowdown.scene: A landing hung with clinic curtains gone stiff with age, a woman folding and refolding a strip of linen
preShowdown.speaker: Sela
dialogue: You look healthy. Good. I've had my fill of the other kind.
The charge on this floor says I spent the last medicine on twelve patients and lost them anyway.
That is accurate. It is not complete. Sit.

preShowdown.title: The Ward
preShowdown.scene: The landing, a long row of empty cots behind the curtains
preShowdown.speaker: Sela
dialogue: That final winter, the sickness didn't behave like sickness. No fever, no rash, no spread I could map. People simply came in empty. Strong men shaking like the last leaf on a branch.
We had one chest of restoratives left in the quarter. Talis wanted it divided thin across everyone. I wanted full doses for the twelve worst.
We argued for two days. Then I took it to the arbitration table and won the right to decide. My deck against hers, in front of the whole ward.

preShowdown.title: The Decision
preShowdown.scene: The landing, her thumb pressed against a dried bloodstain on the curtain edge
preShowdown.speaker: Sela
dialogue: Full doses. The twelve worst. All twelve died with clean dressings on and the medicine still in their blood. Then the rest died slower.
Afterward I said we decided. For four hundred years I have said we. Talis stood at my shoulder through every funeral and never once corrected me in public.
She corrected me in private exactly once. I didn't speak to her for a month. That was my answer.

preShowdown.title: What I Need
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the linen finally set down
preShowdown.speaker: Sela
dialogue: I won the match that made it my decision, so the record says the decision was sound. You see the problem. The table said I was right, and the ward said otherwise.
Play me properly. If the record is going to carry my name alone, let it show these hands were beaten at that table at least once.
One thing before we play. The medicine stayed in their blood, but their strength kept leaving. I had never seen that happen, and I still do not know what a healer could have done with it. Cards.

defeat.title: Pulse Check
defeat.scene: The landing, Sela watching with a clinician's eye
defeat.speaker: Sela
dialogue: Before you go: any pain, blurred vision, ringing ears?
Do not answer quickly. I have watched too many people wave off symptoms just to keep moving.

firstVictory.title: The Second Opinion
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the cards resting like instruments laid down
firstVictory.speaker: Sela
dialogue: There. One loss at my own table, with somebody here to see it.
It changes nothing for the twelve. Say I chose. Go on. I need to hear whether I can stand it in someone else's voice.

firstVictory.title: We
firstVictory.scene: The landing, Sela standing very straight
firstVictory.speaker: Sela
dialogue: Talis did not decide with me. I did. No, that still makes it sound as if I stood alone.
I won the table, opened the chest, and chose the twelve. After they died, I said we in front of the families.
Talis contradicted me once in private. I answered by refusing to speak to her for a month.

firstVictory.title: Discharge
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the curtains stirring though there is no wind
firstVictory.speaker: Sela
dialogue: Understand, I would still argue for the strong dose. That was medicine. It was defensible, and it failed, and failing is a thing medicine does.
Put her name beside the correction. Talis argued to divide the medicine. I overruled her.
Go on up. And eat something before the archive floor. That woman keeps no visiting hours.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.speaker: Sela
dialogue: The tower keeps my rounds now. It never loses a patient. They are all already gone.
Play the memory. Mind the late recoveries. I was always best when it was almost over.

preShowdown.title: The Gate Floor
preShowdown.scene: A landing dominated by a barred district gate, a broad man standing at parade rest before it
preShowdown.speaker: Korin
dialogue: Name and business. Habit. Ignore it.
You want the gate story. Everyone climbs this far for the gate story.
Order forty-one, evacuation stage three. Seal the east lower gate at the second bell and admit no further residents. Signed, the district marshal. I can recite the entire sheet.

preShowdown.title: Word for Word
preShowdown.scene: The landing, his eyes fixed on a point above your head
preShowdown.speaker: Korin
dialogue: You notice that I quote it. I always quote it. If I put it in my own words, it becomes my sentence, and it was never my sentence.
There were people at that gate when the second bell rang. I knew forty of them by name. I closed it on schedule.
A captain who improvises during an evacuation can kill more people than one who obeys. That is true. Let me finish the order before you ask about the names.

preShowdown.title: The Families
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the gate's shadow falling across the table
preShowdown.speaker: Korin
dialogue: The families demanded a Showdown afterward. That was their right. A public table, me answering for the gate.
I refused three times, on procedure. No tables during emergency rule, and the city was under emergency rule.
The emergency outlasted the city. The refusals were lawful. I checked every seal myself.

preShowdown.title: One Detail
preShowdown.scene: The landing, Korin finally looking at you
preShowdown.speaker: Korin
dialogue: Here is the detail that never made a report. The order came down at the second bell. The hill terraces were already empty by the first.
They cleared their own people, and then they sealed mine in. The gate was never about saving the city. It was about choosing which half.
Take the table, then. Four hundred years late, I stand for the gate. Somebody finally answers for it, and it appears to be me.

defeat.title: As Ordered
defeat.scene: The landing, Korin squaring the cards like kit for inspection
defeat.speaker: Korin
dialogue: The result is recorded. That is how a ruling goes, sometimes.
The gate will be here when you return. It is always here.

firstVictory.title: Stand Down
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the bar across the gate looking suddenly like just a piece of iron
firstVictory.speaker: Korin
dialogue: So ruled.
Give me a moment. I have been at attention for a long time.

firstVictory.title: My Own Words
firstVictory.scene: The landing, his voice lower and slower than before
firstVictory.speaker: Korin
dialogue: No order this time. My words.

I closed the gate on my own neighbors because my post fed my family, and my rank kept them on the hill lists. I weighed my two children against forty names I knew, and I chose mine, and I called that choice obedience because obedience has a uniform.
The marshal wrote the order. The hand on the bar was mine.

firstVictory.title: Dismissed
firstVictory.scene: The landing, Korin at rest for the first time
firstVictory.speaker: Korin
dialogue: I do not ask forgiveness. The forty cannot give it, and nobody else holds it.
But I have finally said it without the marshal's words in my mouth. I should have done that while someone outside the gate was still alive to hear it.
Go up. When someone above me explains why the order existed, remember that I still lifted the bar and set it in place.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.scene: The landing, the gate barred again
rematch.speaker: Korin
dialogue: The tower holds the gate now. Word for word, bar for bar.
Challenge the memory when you like. It follows the order exactly, even when the gate should stay open.

preShowdown.title: The Archive Floor
preShowdown.scene: A landing of scorched shelving, ash settled in even grey drifts, a composed woman with ink-stained cuffs
preShowdown.speaker: Nima
dialogue: Mind the ash. It is all catalogued, in its way.
You have climbed six floors of people who wanted their stories corrected. I am the one who decided which stories existed at all.
History remembers me as the woman who burned the last records of the Court. History is working from incomplete sources. I saw to that personally.

preShowdown.title: What Burned
preShowdown.scene: The landing, her hand hovering over an empty shelf without touching it
preShowdown.speaker: Nima
dialogue: The night the Court came apart, the registry held two kinds of paper.

The first was shelter lists. Every hidden cellar, every family inside them. Certain officials wanted those lists, and not so they could bring anyone soup. I burned them, and I would burn them again tonight.
That is the version I tell. It has the advantage of being true.

preShowdown.title: The Other Paper
preShowdown.scene: The landing, ash stirring in a draft from below
preShowdown.speaker: Nima
dialogue: The other paper belonged to an investigator named Corvale. He had spent two years measuring what the works below actually consumed against what the city received back.
The numbers did not meet. Something between the intake and the lamps was drinking the difference, and his figures showed exactly how much. He gave me the only copy for safekeeping.
It went into the same fire as the shelter lists. One armful. Very efficient.

preShowdown.title: The Family
preShowdown.scene: The landing, Nima seated with a deck squared before her like a verdict
preShowdown.speaker: Nima
dialogue: His family challenged me at the table when he disappeared. They knew he had trusted me. I refused the match, and I outlived the schedule.
Understand the shape of it. I did not burn his figures to protect the shelters. I burned them because the council would have asked how I came to be holding them.
His daughter stood in the registry doorway for three days. I worked at my desk and did not look up. Now you know exactly what you are playing. Shall we?

defeat.title: Filed
defeat.scene: The landing, a small tidy notation made in ash
defeat.speaker: Nima
dialogue: Recorded. Loss, challenger, floor seven. I keep tidy books even now.
Come back when you have revised. The ash is not going anywhere.

firstVictory.title: Reopened
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the burned shelves looking more like ribs than furniture
firstVictory.speaker: Nima
dialogue: A fair table. Corvale's family asked me for one, and I said no.
You sat down when I asked. I could have done the same for them.

firstVictory.title: Restitution
firstVictory.scene: The landing, her cuffs pushed back, ink stains old and permanent
firstVictory.speaker: Nima
dialogue: I know how I would file this: the four hundred sheltered first, Corvale in an appendix. No. I did that for four hundred years.
Start again. Corvale, registry investigator. His figures were correct. He trusted me with the only copy, and I burned it.
Then Ise. She waited three days for an answer I would not give.

firstVictory.title: Shelved
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the drifts of ash undisturbed
firstVictory.speaker: Nima
dialogue: Put me after them. Do not let my office put me first again.
I have no amendment that makes the fire smaller. Only the order of the names.
The Chronicle Arbiter waits on floor eight. Ask him what he certified as fair.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.scene: The landing, the catalog reordered overnight
rematch.speaker: Nima
dialogue: The tower will not let me rearrange this collection. I have tested.
Come back whenever you like. The ash will tell the same story.

preShowdown.title: The Hall of Record
preShowdown.scene: A landing built like a tribunal hall, an empty witness table, a silver-haired man in an arbiter's sash
preShowdown.speaker: Eren
dialogue: You have been climbing through my caseload. Tovin's postponement. Korin's refusals. The healer's arbitration. Every table in this city ran on my rulings, one way or another.
I was the Chronicle Arbiter. When a Showdown touched the public record, I certified it fair.
Sit. You are about to hear the word fair do some heavy lifting.

preShowdown.title: The Question
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the benches of the hall empty and listening
preShowdown.speaker: Eren
dialogue: In the last years, an engineer demanded a public table on one question. Whether the Hollow Gate was safe.
There. I have said the name. Seven floors of people calling it the works, the intake, the machine below. It was called the Hollow Gate, and asking about it out loud was treated as a kind of arson.
The council could not refuse her the table. Refusal would confirm everything. So they came to me instead.

preShowdown.title: The Conditions
preShowdown.scene: The landing, Eren laying out cards with a court official's precision
preShowdown.speaker: Eren
dialogue: I set her opponent. A tournament killer from outside the district, briefed on her deck beforehand. I ruled her key evidence inadmissible until after the match, on a formality I invented that same morning.
And the result was drafted before either deck was shuffled. I initialed the draft myself. Fair, certified.
She played better than the whole hall expected. It very nearly did not matter that we had fixed it. Very nearly.

preShowdown.title: The Defense
preShowdown.scene: The landing, his voice level, his hands perfectly still
preShowdown.speaker: Eren
dialogue: Bought is the simpler version. I was never bought.

I believed the panic would kill more people than the Gate. Say out loud, on the record, that the Gate is eating the city, and you get riots, hoarding, the lower wards burning the upper ones. I had seen bread panics. I did the arithmetic of fear, and I ruled for quiet.
The city died anyway, of the very thing she tried to say. So my arithmetic protected nothing except the schedule of the dying.

preShowdown.title: The Vacant Chair
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the witness table waiting
preShowdown.speaker: Eren
dialogue: Her table was never honestly played. That is the open entry on this floor. You will stand in for the challenger, and I will play the match I should have certified.
No arranged opponent. No sealed evidence. One fair table, four hundred years late, against the man who made certain there was not one.
I still believe the panic would have been a massacre. Hold that against me while you deal.

defeat.title: Certified
defeat.scene: The landing, Eren filing the result with visible distaste for his own habit
defeat.speaker: Eren
dialogue: A clean loss. Note the novelty. Every result I certified was clean on paper too.
The procedure worked today. Come and test it again.

firstVictory.title: Overturned
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the hall very quiet
firstVictory.speaker: Eren
dialogue: So that is how a fair match looks when nobody is holding the scales.
It cannot tell me whether Lyra would have won that day. That uncertainty is what I stole when I fixed her table.

firstVictory.title: The Ruling
firstVictory.scene: The landing, Eren removing his sash and folding it once
firstVictory.speaker: Eren
dialogue: Enter this over my seal. The Showdown of the engineer Lyra was decided before the decks were presented. The arbiter of record certified a fiction, knowingly, in the stated interest of public order.
I do not withdraw the reasoning. Panic kills. I have watched it work. I withdraw the certificate.
There is a difference between a wrong ruling and a false one. I could have survived being wrong.

firstVictory.title: Adjourned
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the sash left on the witness table
firstVictory.speaker: Eren
dialogue: She is one floor up. Give her the table I owed her.
When she tells you what the Gate was doing, remember that I held her evidence before I sealed it away.
The Gate did not bribe or threaten me. The council asked for quiet, and I gave that request the weight of law.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.speaker: Eren
dialogue: The tower convenes this court now. Its certifications are, at last, accurate.
Retry the case at will. This time the verdict waits for the cards.

preShowdown.title: The Engine Floor
preShowdown.scene: A landing crossed with dead conduits, a faint light still crawling inside one of them, a woman with burn-scarred hands
preShowdown.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: Eren sent you up. Did he apologize? Don't tell me. His apologies read like contracts. I have signed enough of his paper.
You know my name if you played his table. The engineer. The saboteur, in the official record.
I stabilized the Hollow Gate for eleven years. Sabotage would have been the better career.

preShowdown.title: What It Was
preShowdown.scene: The landing, her scarred palm flat against a cold conduit
preShowdown.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: The Court built the Gate. Our own engineers sank it under the ridge to end famine, war, and winter for good, and I was on the crew that finished the work.
It gave us everything. Water pressure, cold stores, light without smoke, healing wards that closed wounds overnight. We hung the entire city on it and called ourselves clever.
Every system we hung on it made it harder to ever take down.

preShowdown.title: The Draw
preShowdown.scene: The landing, the one live conduit pulsing slow, like breath
preShowdown.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: Here is what I measured, and what they buried.
The Gate put out less than it took in, and the gap widened every year. The intake was not coal and it was not water, because I metered both, and the figures laughed at me.

It was drawing on the people. Chakra, vigor, whatever word you use for the thing that gets a man up a ladder. The work crews below went first because they stood closest. The whole lower city was standing in the shallow end of the same drain.

preShowdown.title: My Part
preShowdown.scene: The landing, Lyra rolling up her sleeves out of old habit
preShowdown.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: Now the part I rehearsed for four hundred years and never got to say at a fair table.
I saw the early signs in year three. Tremor in the crews. The draw curve bending the wrong way. I had standing, I had the data, and I had a career built on that machine being a miracle.

I wrote acceptable variance in the margin. Three winters running. By the time I wrote anything else, the city could not live without the thing that was eating it, and the council had a man like Eren for people like me.

preShowdown.title: The Fair Table
preShowdown.scene: The landing, a deck laid out on a workbench between tools
preShowdown.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: They gave me a rigged match and entered my numbers as sabotage. You are here to play the match that should have happened.
Fair warning. I play like the Gate. Big output, ugly costs, everything unstable. I built the deck that way on purpose. I had a long time to think about the design.
Whatever you have brought. Let me see it.

defeat.title: Overload
defeat.scene: The landing, the workbench humming faintly
defeat.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: The rig held. That is the result, however much I dislike the simplicity.
I will reset the table. Come back when you are ready.

firstVictory.title: Shutdown
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the last live conduit finally dark
firstVictory.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: There. Unstable by design. It only ever has to hold a little longer, and it never, ever does.
That is the honest result. Mine this time. Not the one Eren printed.

firstVictory.title: The Admission
firstVictory.scene: The landing, Lyra looking at her scars without flinching
firstVictory.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: Then here is what the Court left out.

I measured what the Gate was taking before the council was willing to name it. Then I spent the three winters when shutdown was still survivable calling the evidence acceptable variance, because the miracle had my name on it.
The sabotage charge was false. The three years I wasted were real.

firstVictory.title: For the Record
firstVictory.scene: The landing, the tools laid out in a neat row, waiting for no one
firstVictory.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: Do not give the Gate intentions. We built a machine that drew from whoever stood nearest, then kept sending the same people near it.
The man above me kept it fed. He will explain himself beautifully. He always did.
Listen anyway. Somebody finally should.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: The tower runs my rig now, and I cannot write acceptable variance in its margin.
Stress it as often as you like. The same fault will still be there.

preShowdown.title: The Council Floor
preShowdown.scene: The tower's high chamber, a long table set for a full council, one grey man seated alone at its head
preShowdown.speaker: Halden
dialogue: You have met my city on your way up. The bell keeper. The clerk. My captain, my arbiter, my engineer.
I could give you a defense for every one of them. I required those defenses in writing and accepted them because they kept the city moving.
Sit. You are the first person to reach this table in four hundred years who does not owe me anything.

preShowdown.title: What I Knew
preShowdown.scene: The chamber, the empty council chairs ranked down the table
preShowdown.speaker: Halden
dialogue: Let us dispose of the mystery early. I knew. From Lyra's third report onward, I knew what the Gate was drawing, and from whom.
People imagine a chancellor deceived by his ministers. I was the best-informed man in the Court. Every floor below you crossed this desk as a number.
The question was never knowledge. It was what would fail first if I ordered a shutdown.

preShowdown.title: The Ledger
preShowdown.scene: The chamber, Halden turning a single page as if it weighs a great deal
preShowdown.speaker: Halden
dialogue: Turn the Gate off, and by the fourth day the pumps stop, and the high cisterns hold three days of water. The cold stores fail, and half a winter's food spoils in a week. The healing wards go dark with four hundred people inside them.
Every one of those figures was real. I checked each one twice because I wanted one of them to be false.

In the first winter, shutting it down meant a thousand dead within days. Keeping it on meant tremors, missing names, and sick workers spread across the city. I chose the harm that did not arrive all at once. Then I made the same choice for eleven years.

preShowdown.title: The Machinery
preShowdown.scene: The chamber, the lamps burning steady while the city in the windows stands dark
preShowdown.speaker: Halden
dialogue: Understand what the days cost, though. Each one needed quiet, and quiet needed work.

A dry aqueduct filed as maintenance. A grain ledger adjusted. An engineer discredited, an arbiter leaned on, a district sealed by its own captain's hands. None of it felt like ruin. It felt like the morning's memoranda.

Each day I postponed the shutdown, one more pump, storehouse, or ward came to depend on the Gate. An order made quickly for the sake of a clean conscience would still have left those people without water, food, or light.

preShowdown.title: The Witness
preShowdown.scene: The chamber, Halden rising to deal with his own hands
preShowdown.speaker: Halden
dialogue: I kept the Chronicle close all those years. Chose its arbiters, scheduled its tables, postponed every one with my name in it. History would judge me, I liked to say, having appointed history personally.
Then this tower kept my memory without asking my permission. I find I have no argument against that.
You chose none of this and owe none of it. Play the last table of the Sunken Court, and let the record close honestly for once.

defeat.title: Another Day
defeat.scene: The chamber, Halden gathering the cards with terrible patience
defeat.speaker: Halden
dialogue: And that is how it is done. One more day, purchased. It is a very old trick of mine.
Note that it cost you nothing but an afternoon. I never once got the price that low.

firstVictory.title: Adjourned
firstVictory.scene: The chamber, the final card face up, the lamps steady
firstVictory.speaker: Halden
dialogue: There it is.
Forty years of appointed history, and the record closes on a table I did not schedule, against a witness I did not choose. Good.

firstVictory.title: The Truth of It
firstVictory.scene: The chamber, Halden seated back in the head chair, smaller in it now
firstVictory.speaker: Halden
dialogue: Here is the confession, then. Mind, it is not the one people expect.

There was never a day when shutting it down looked merciful. In the first winter I saw a thousand immediate deaths on one side and smaller harms scattered across the city on the other. I chose what I could explain at the next council meeting.

By the end, the pumps still ran and the lamps still burned, but workers came up shaking and whole districts had been abandoned. Every proposal to stop forced me to answer for the years I had already delayed. I kept those proposals out of the room.

firstVictory.title: The Verdict
firstVictory.scene: The chamber, the windows full of a city that stopped
firstVictory.speaker: Halden
dialogue: Do not write that the Gate destroyed us in a night. Nothing so honest. It dimmed us for a generation while we called the dimming necessary.

It drank the strong, dried the channels, starved the kilns, sealed the gates, bought the tables, and set neighbor against neighbor over grain. And at every step it offered the same bargain. One more day. We took that bargain every single time, and I signed for it.
I had eleven years to order a shutdown. Each year the cost was higher, and each year I used that as my reason to wait. You have seen what I did.

firstVictory.title: The Record Closes
firstVictory.scene: The chamber, Halden looking down the long table at the empty chairs
firstVictory.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: He looks down the table for a while, at the chairs, at whatever he still sees in them.
Then he straightens the last page, and leaves it face up.

firstVictory.title: Adjournment
firstVictory.scene: The chamber, quiet
firstVictory.speaker: Halden
dialogue: Tell the floors below that the session finally ended. Tovin first. He waited longest at his post.
The chamber is yours, witness. We are, at last, adjourned.

rematch.title: Replay the Memory
rematch.scene: The chamber, the head chair occupied by lamplight
rematch.speaker: Halden
dialogue: The tower convenes the session without me now. It sits at the head of the table and offers the same bargain I did.
Refuse it as often as you like. That was only ever the vote that mattered.

echoes-age-1.title: The Lowest Floors
echoes-age-1.scene: The white fox Shiranui sits at a tower window, a dust-grey quarter of the fallen city below at dusk
echoes-age-1.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You wanted to understand the machine under your villages. Good. Then you have to understand who built it, and what it did to them first.
This tower keeps the Sunken Court. Not the dead of it. The memories. The way the Chronicle keeps a page after the hand that wrote it is gone.
Start at the bottom, with the people the Court blamed first. A bell keeper. A grain seller. A girl who ran messages.

echoes-age-1.title: What the Gate Took First
echoes-age-1.scene: The quarter below, lamps failing one by one along a street
echoes-age-1.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: The Court built the Hollow Gate to end famine and winter, and at first it did. Then it began to take more than it gave.
It does not hunger. It measures. It took from the bottom of the city first, quietly, where the people had the least to spare and the least voice to say so.
Bells failed. Grain went short. Water dried in the low wards. It all looked like ordinary bad luck, and ordinary people carried the blame for it.

echoes-age-1.title: Why They Linger
echoes-age-1.scene: The tower landing, a single worn table waiting
echoes-age-1.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: Each floor holds a challenge left unanswered. Tovin was promised his table. Doran and Aya issued theirs. Not one was ever held.
So the Chronicle preserved each accusation as if nobody had ever disputed it.
That is why they linger. Not for revenge. For the answer they were owed and never given.

echoes-age-1.title: Sit Down
echoes-age-1.scene: The table, two seats, your deck in your hands
echoes-age-1.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You cannot give them back their city. You can do the one thing the Court would not.
You can show up, and let them finish.
Go on. One table at a time.

echoes-age-2.title: The Middle Floors
echoes-age-2.scene: Shiranui pads along a gallery above shuttered halls of records and offices
echoes-age-2.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: Climb, and the memories change. They stop being the blamed and start being the ones who did the blaming.
A clerk who moved the numbers. A healer who chose who the last medicine would save. A captain who sealed a gate on his own neighbors.
They were ordinary officials with a duty, enough authority to make one choice hold, and a reason ready when anyone asked.

echoes-age-2.title: The Ledgers That Learned to Lie
echoes-age-2.scene: A hall of pigeonhole shelves, one entry scraped clean
echoes-age-2.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: The clues were divided among them. Ansel saw impossible ration demand below the city. Sela saw full doses remain in patients' blood while their strength failed. Korin knew the hill wards were emptied before he sealed the lower gate.
Those facts did not yet add up to the Gate's drain. They did show who kept paying for every official decision.
So the records learned to lie, one careful correction at a time, and the truth was filed where no one would think to look.

echoes-age-2.title: Why They Linger
echoes-age-2.scene: The sealed official gate, wax seals gone grey
echoes-age-2.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: Every one of them can explain themselves. That is the trouble. Each decision sounds reasonable, heard alone.
None of them was ever made to say it all out loud, in order, at a fair table, while someone wrote it down.
So they linger with their explanations still folded in their pockets, waiting for someone who will not accept the short version. That someone is you.

echoes-age-3.title: The Upper Floors
echoes-age-3.scene: Shiranui at a high parapet, the tribunal dome and a distant machine leaking faint teal light beyond
echoes-age-3.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: Near the top, the memories belong to the ones who could have stopped it. And to the machine itself.

An archivist who burned the evidence rather than let it be read. An arbiter who fixed a public Showdown. And an engineer who hid her first warnings for three winters before she finally tried to make the danger public.
This is the age when the Hollow Gate finally had a name spoken aloud, and speaking it aloud became a crime. Each of these three helped the silence last.

echoes-age-3.title: Whose Machine It Was
echoes-age-3.scene: A workbench of dead conduits, one still faintly lit
echoes-age-3.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: Hold onto whose machine it was. The Court sank the Gate under its own ridge, with its own engineers, to end its own winters. Nobody found it. They made it.
When one of those engineers came back to say it was eating the people, the Court did not deny the Gate. It denied her.
A rigged table, an unfair opponent, a verdict written before the decks were dealt. That was cheaper than the truth.

echoes-age-3.title: Why They Linger
echoes-age-3.scene: The empty witness table under the dome
echoes-age-3.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: They linger because every chance to put the truth before witnesses was refused or fixed.
One family never got its challenge. Lyra got a verdict written before her cards were dealt. Eren signed it.
You cannot recover the answer that table would have given. You can refuse the Court's false one and hear what each of them did.

echoes-age-4.title: The Highest Floor
echoes-age-4.scene: Shiranui at the doors of a high council palace, one lit window against a dead unlit city at night
echoes-age-4.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: One floor remains, and one memory. The last chancellor of the Sunken Court. I will wait out here for this one.
He was not deceived. He knew exactly what the Gate was doing, and he kept it running anyway. Let him tell you why before you decide what to call him.
One more day, he decided. Then he decided it again, until there were no days left to decide.

echoes-age-4.title: Why He Lingers
echoes-age-4.scene: The long council table beyond the doors, every chair empty but one
echoes-age-4.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: He said history would judge him. Then he made certain it could not, by keeping the record in his own hands.
Every arbiter he chose. Every table he scheduled. Every Showdown with his name on it that he quietly postponed until there was no city left to hold it.
So he lingers at the head of a table no one was ever allowed to sit across from.

echoes-age-4.title: The Witness He Could Not Choose
echoes-age-4.scene: The head chair, a single lamp, your deck on the table
echoes-age-4.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You are the one thing he never accounted for. A witness he did not appoint, cannot dismiss, and does not control.
Sit down across from the man who governed a city that was already gone. Close the last page of the Sunken Court honestly, for the first time.
Then come back down, and remember what he chose. Four intakes are feeding the Gate under your villages right now. Remember how ordinary one more day sounded here.

prompt.title: The First Record
prompt.scene: The lowest landing, Shiranui beside three open Chronicle pages
prompt.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: That is all these floors can give you: a severed bell rope, grain carried to a shelter, and a dry aqueduct. The people disagree about the rest.
Before we climb, decide how you will carry their account. You can amend it later in your own mind. The tower will keep the first answer you put on the page.

choices.label: Record the warnings
choices.record: The record begins with the cut rope, the shelter grain, and the dry aqueduct. The accusations remain attached as claims, not conclusions.

choices.label: Keep their names first
choices.record: Tovin, Doran, and Aya remain at the head of the record. Their contradictions stay beside their names instead of being smoothed away.

choices.label: Leave the cause open
choices.record: The three warnings are preserved together, but the record does not claim that these witnesses alone knew what caused them.

denied-attack.title: What the Table Kept
denied-attack.scene: Aya gathers the cards, one stopped attack still bright in the Chronicle
denied-attack.speaker: Aya
dialogue: You stopped one clean. Good. The Chronicle can keep that without pretending it explains the road I left.

recovered-ground.title: What the Table Kept
recovered-ground.scene: Aya gathers the cards as the Chronicle holds the moment the line steadied
recovered-ground.speaker: Aya
dialogue: You took the hit and your line came back. That happened here. It does not make my old choice yours.

rebuilt-line.title: What the Table Kept
rebuilt-line.scene: Aya gathers the cards as a fallen place on the table fills again
rebuilt-line.speaker: Aya
dialogue: You lost a card and put another body in its place. The tower saw it. That is enough for this match.

unrecorded.title: What the Table Kept
unrecorded.scene: Aya gathers the cards while the Chronicle settles
unrecorded.speaker: Aya
dialogue: The tower kept the match whole. One table cannot tell you why I left that road. Ask the pages for that.

warnings-first.title: What You Carried Up
warnings-first.scene: Shiranui touches one claw to the three warnings entered on the open page
warnings-first.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You put the warnings first. Up here, watch what officials did when warnings reached a desk.

names-first.title: What You Carried Up
names-first.scene: Shiranui glances down toward the three names written at the head of the page
names-first.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You kept their names ahead of the theory. Up here, names start disappearing behind offices and seals.

cause-open.title: What You Carried Up
cause-open.scene: Shiranui closes the first page without fastening it
cause-open.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You left the cause open. Good. These next witnesses knew more, but no one on this floor held the whole answer either.

haldenAcknowledgements.warnings-first: You entered the cut rope, the missing grain, and the dry channel before you entered a cause. My offices had all three reports.
haldenAcknowledgements.names-first: You kept Tovin, Doran, and Aya where an office could not turn them into a shortage report. Mine did exactly that.
haldenAcknowledgements.cause-open: You refused to make three low-floor witnesses name a cause they could not see. I could see it from this chair.

prompt.title: The Official Record
prompt.scene: The middle landing, three office seals laid beside an open Chronicle page
prompt.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: Ansel changed a figure. Sela spent the medicine. Korin closed the gate. Each had a reason, and each reason left someone else to bear the result.
How should the page hold acts that are certain when responsibility is still argued?

choices.label: Separate acts from reasons
choices.record: The altered figure, spent medicine, and sealed gate are recorded before the explanations offered for them. Both remain visible.

choices.label: Index who paid
choices.record: The record follows the ration crews, untreated patients, and people outside the gate, while preserving the officials' stated reasons beside the cost.

choices.label: Leave duty unresolved
choices.record: The orders and choices are preserved without settling where duty ended and personal responsibility began.

denied-attack.title: Entered in Order
denied-attack.scene: Korin squares the discard pile while a stopped attack remains in the Chronicle
denied-attack.speaker: Korin
dialogue: You denied an attack before it landed. The table records the act and its time. It says nothing about the order I did receive, or why I obeyed it.

recovered-ground.title: Entered in Order
recovered-ground.scene: Korin squares the discard pile at the point the challenger recovered
recovered-ground.speaker: Korin
dialogue: Your line recovered after damage. That is in the match record. It does not reopen a gate already closed.

rebuilt-line.title: Entered in Order
rebuilt-line.scene: Korin squares the discard pile beside a rebuilt line
rebuilt-line.speaker: Korin
dialogue: A card fell and you summoned again. Clear sequence. Keep the same precision when you write what happened outside my gate.

unrecorded.title: Entered in Order
unrecorded.scene: Korin squares the discard pile while the Chronicle seals the match
unrecorded.speaker: Korin
dialogue: The match is recorded. Do not make it carry testimony it never heard.

acts-and-excuses.title: What You Carried Up
acts-and-excuses.scene: Shiranui turns the page so the acts remain above the explanations
acts-and-excuses.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You kept the acts apart from the reasons. On these floors, people worked to destroy the act, the reason, or anyone who joined them.

who-paid.title: What You Carried Up
who-paid.scene: Shiranui traces the margin where the people who bore each decision are named
who-paid.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You followed the people who paid. Now follow the evidence their suffering produced, and who made sure it would not travel.

duty-open.title: What You Carried Up
duty-open.scene: Shiranui leaves the question of duty uncrossed at the bottom of the page
duty-open.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You left duty unsettled. The people above had more authority and better evidence. That changes the question, but it does not answer it for you.

haldenAcknowledgements.acts-and-excuses: You separated what my officials did from what they said afterward. I approved both the acts and the language used to defend them.
haldenAcknowledgements.who-paid: You indexed the lower wards, the patients, and the people outside Korin's gate. Every one of them crossed my desk as a number. That was how I let myself count.
haldenAcknowledgements.duty-open: You left room to ask where duty ended. I spent years moving that boundary whenever it reached my desk.

prompt.title: The Suppressed Record
prompt.scene: The upper landing, ash, an arbiter's seal, and Lyra's figures on one table
prompt.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: Nima burned shelter lists to protect families, then burned Corvale's proof to hide why she held it. Eren certified a table he knew was fixed. Lyra hid early warnings, then tried to expose the Gate and was silenced.
The facts meet here, but they do not become one simple kind of guilt. What will your page refuse to lose?

choices.label: Trace proof and silence
choices.record: The record traces what evidence existed, who could read it, and each point where it was burned, fixed, withheld, or finally spoken.

choices.label: Keep culpability divided
choices.record: Protection, fear, ambition, delay, and suppression remain attached to the people who chose them. The record does not compress them into one excuse or one crime.

choices.label: Leave the lost verdict open
choices.record: The fixed Showdown is recorded as fraud. The page does not pretend a later fair match can prove what Lyra's lost table would have decided.

denied-attack.title: A Clean Observation
denied-attack.scene: Lyra watches the Chronicle hold one denied attack in pale teal lines
denied-attack.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: The denial registered before impact. Useful. It proves the safeguard worked here, once. No more than that.

recovered-ground.title: A Clean Observation
recovered-ground.scene: Lyra watches the Chronicle trace damage and recovery on the same line
recovered-ground.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: The line fell and recovered. Record both values. Recovery does not erase the load that caused it.

rebuilt-line.title: A Clean Observation
rebuilt-line.scene: Lyra watches a destroyed card followed by a new summon in the Chronicle
rebuilt-line.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: Loss, then replacement. The second event did not undo the first. My reports should have said that plainly.

unrecorded.title: A Clean Observation
unrecorded.scene: Lyra watches the completed match resolve into a quiet page
unrecorded.speaker: Lyra
dialogue: Keep the match as a match. My figures have their own burden of proof.

proof-and-silence.title: What You Carried Up
proof-and-silence.scene: Shiranui looks from the burned figures to the council doors above
proof-and-silence.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You traced where proof stopped moving. The man behind those doors controlled the last places it could have gone.

divided-culpability.title: What You Carried Up
divided-culpability.scene: Shiranui closes three separate files and leaves their names visible
divided-culpability.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You kept their culpability divided. Halden will try to gather every choice into the weight of his office. Listen for what was still his.

outcome-open.title: What You Carried Up
outcome-open.scene: Shiranui leaves the false verdict crossed out and the lost one blank
outcome-open.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: You did not replace Eren's false verdict with one of your own. Halden knows what he did without help from a match that never happened.

haldenAcknowledgements.proof-and-silence: You followed the figures through the fire, the fixed table, and Lyra's testimony. They stopped at doors I controlled.
haldenAcknowledgements.divided-culpability: You kept the people below from becoming one convenient culprit. I cannot distribute my signature among them.
haldenAcknowledgements.outcome-open: You left Lyra's stolen verdict unwritten. Fair. My decision to suppress her does not depend on guessing how her match would have ended.

prompt.title: The Last Entry
prompt.scene: Outside the council chamber, Shiranui waits beside Halden's final page
prompt.speaker: Shiranui
dialogue: Halden has given you his reasons and his eleven years of delay. The city still fell as it fell. This is only the question of how his testimony enters the record.
What must a reader meet before the page closes?

choices.label: Enter every delay
choices.record: The record treats each postponed shutdown as a decision made with the knowledge available that year, not as one choice made only at the end.

choices.label: Keep cost beside harm
choices.record: The deaths feared in an immediate shutdown remain beside the workers, districts, and channels consumed while the Gate continued.

choices.label: Close without a verdict
choices.record: Halden's knowledge, authority, delays, and stated reasons are sealed as testimony. The final judgment is left to whoever reads it.

denied-attack.title: Entered into Session
denied-attack.scene: Halden watches the Chronicle preserve a denied attack
denied-attack.speaker: Halden
dialogue: A refusal entered before the damage. I entered too few of those in my own record. The match records this one without acquitting anyone.

recovered-ground.title: Entered into Session
recovered-ground.scene: Halden watches damage and recovery settle into the Chronicle
recovered-ground.speaker: Halden
dialogue: You recovered after the damage. Administrations adore that word. The Chronicle is less forgiving. It keeps the damage too.

rebuilt-line.title: Entered into Session
rebuilt-line.scene: Halden watches a new summon take a lost card's place
rebuilt-line.speaker: Halden
dialogue: You filled an empty place. I did that for years and called the board intact. The Chronicle, at least, keeps what was lost.

unrecorded.title: Entered into Session
unrecorded.scene: Halden watches the Chronicle close around the finished match
unrecorded.speaker: Halden
dialogue: Let the match certify only that it was held. My record does not need a victory to become true.
